chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
"There is no harm if a man pours out his water (or empties his vessel) at night if he is afraid."
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pour out water or perform ablution at night if one is afraid?
ai.summary: In the context of the Miqat of Muzdalifah during Hajj, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) grants legal flexibility (rukhsah) for performing wudu or ghusl at night when fear of enemies or danger is present. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'al-khuruj min al-dar' (exiting the state of strict obligation due to necessity), prioritizing safety and ease over the preferred time of nightfall, reflecting the practical realities of early Muslim pilgrims.
